proposals.before: He then turned his forces elsewhere and captured the Governor of Yunzhong, Su, along with the chancellor jisi and the general Xun.
proposals.after: He then turned his forces elsewhere and captured the Governor of Yunzhong, Su, along with the chancellor Ji Si and the general Xun.
proposals.reason: Personal name 箕肆 should be capitalized as Ji Si, not lowercase jisi.

proposals.before: appointed Hedong governor Yafu as general, stationed at Xiliu: to prepare against the Xiongnu.
proposals.after: appointed Henei governor Yafu as general, stationed at Xiliu: to prepare against the Xiongnu.
proposals.reason: Chinese 河內守 is Henei, not Hedong (河東); idiomatic already has Henei.

proposals.before: Even yiyin and the Duke of Zhou could scarcely have done more!
proposals.after: Even Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou could scarcely have done more!
proposals.reason: 伊尹 should be rendered Yi Yin with standard capitalization, not lowercase yiyin.

proposals.before: Even yiyin and Zhou Gong, what could surpass this!
proposals.after: Even Yi Yin and Zhou Gong, what could surpass this!
proposals.reason: 伊尹 should be Yi Yin in the literal English as well.

decisions.reason: 丞相箕肆 names the chancellor 箕肆; lowercase "jisi" misformats that personal name, and "Ji Si" restores standard capitalization without changing meaning.
The Chinese has 河內守, which is Henei, not Hedong (河東); the literal's "Hedong" is a place-name error, and the idiomatic already correctly has Henei.
伊尹 is the personal name Yi Yin; lowercase "yiyin" is an incorrect rendering of that name, and "Yi Yin" matches standard English usage alongside 周公 as the Duke of Zhou.
The same 伊尹 in the literal must be "Yi Yin," not lowercase "yiyin"; the proposed fix corrects the name without altering the rest of the calque.
